title: Apply Compliance Fixes
bottom_line: After you answer the audit's planning questions, one command turns each open in-repo card into its own merged pull request, one card at a time.

sections.heading: Answer the planning questions, then type one command

blocks.caption: Run it from the root of the audited repo, after `/compliance-audit:audit` has published its report and you have answered the planning questions on that page.

blocks.title: What you can add after the command
rows: The newest compliance audit for the current repo. It asks you if none or several match.
The model that plans each fix
The model that implements, reviews, tests and resolves merge conflicts
The `default_base_branch` setting; when that is empty, the repository's default branch
The branch each pull request goes to. Every card branches from it and merges into it.
The start of each card's branch name

blocks.title: Example: implement the open cards against a develop branch

blocks.text: You can also ask in plain words, such as "apply the audit", "fix the compliance cards", "implement the legal changes" or "I answered the questions, go". It does not run the audit itself; use `audit` for that.

sections.heading: Set up GitHub access and ntfy before you start

cards.title: Claude Code with Artifacts
cards.text: Artifacts must be enabled. It reads the report back from the claude.ai Artifact page.

cards.title: git and GitHub CLI
cards.text: `git`, and the GitHub CLI (`gh`) signed in with push access.

cards.title: Auto-merge on the repo
cards.text: Auto-merge must be enabled on the repository.

cards.title: ntfy server setting
cards.text: It sends push notifications through the `ntfy` plugin, so set the ntfy `server` setting first.

cards.title: Python 3
cards.text: For the card-reading script, which uses only the standard library.

blocks.text: It drives the `plan-tools` plugin (`split-plan`, `plan-split-implment`, `finalize-pr`) and the `ntfy` plugin. Both are installed together with compliance-audit. No environment variables are needed.

blocks.title: The one setting
rows: The branch `apply` opens pull requests against when you do not pass `--base`. Empty means the repository's default branch.

blocks.title: Change the setting with
blocks.caption: A setting only takes effect after you open the settings dialog and save it once.

sections.heading: Cards run in dependency order, with legal documents last

blocks.title: Which cards it picks up
blocks.caption: Fixes outside the repo are store consoles, registrations and lawyer review.

blocks.text: Legal documents come last because they describe what the product does. The privacy policy, terms, cookie policy, DPA, sub-processor list, imprint, accessibility statement and store privacy labels wait for the cards that change what they describe.

Before starting, it prints the order as one line per card, then starts without waiting. For a card shared between owners, it implements the repo part and lists the rest in the pull request description.

sections.heading: Each card becomes one pull request that merges on its own

steps.title: Plan
steps.text: An Opus subagent plans from the card and your saved answers. It asks you anything they do not settle.

steps.title: Implement
steps.text: Sonnet subagents implement it (`/plan-tools:plan-split-implment` when the plan was split).

steps.title: Fix what they surface
steps.text: Anything they surface is fixed on the same branch, never opened as a follow-up issue.

steps.title: Review and raise the PR
steps.text: `/plan-tools:finalize-pr` reviews, runs the test plan once and raises the pull request against `--base`, with the results in its description.

steps.title: Auto-merge and wait
steps.text: The pull request is set to squash auto-merge and the skill waits for the merge. It merges the base branch back in whenever it moves.

steps.title: Mark Done
steps.text: The card is marked Done on the report and the next card starts.

blocks.title: Built-in defaults
rows: Plans with Opus and implements with Sonnet
Each card gets a branch named `compliance/<card>`
Each card's pull request is set to squash auto-merge and the skill waits for the merge
Pull requests go to the repository's default branch

blocks.title: What you allow by running it
items: For the whole run it may create branches, commit, push, open pull requests against the base branch, edit their descriptions, enable auto-merge, merge the base branch into the card branch, and update card statuses on the report. It does not stop to confirm these.
It leaves GitHub issues that existed before the run alone. It does not implement, close, comment on or reference them.

sections.heading: It runs unattended and pings your phone when stuck

cards.title: Auto-merge disabled
cards.text: The repository does not allow auto-merge.

cards.title: A check keeps failing
cards.text: The same check failed three times.

cards.title: Review needed for hours
cards.text: The pull request is still open after 6 hours.

cards.title: Needs a product decision
cards.text: A merge conflict it cannot resolve without one.

cards.title: Credentials or console access
cards.text: The fix needs your own access.

cards.title: Someone else's changes
cards.text: The working tree has changes that are not its own.

blocks.text: Apart from planning questions, it works without you. When stuck, it sends an ntfy push at priority 4, tells you in chat what is blocked and what it needs, and waits. It does not skip to the next card, because later cards may depend on this one.

sections.heading: Re-running picks up where it stopped

before.label: First run stopped
before.text: For example, a first run stopped with some cards marked Done and one card's pull request still open.

after.label: Run it again
after.text: Done cards are skipped and open card pull requests are picked up where they were.

sections.heading: The final reply lists what merged and what is left

cards.title: Merged cards
cards.text: When every card is merged or set aside, the reply lists each merged card as `#id title` with its pull request link.

cards.title: Cards set aside
cards.text: Fixes outside the repo, each with its owner and the exact action left.

cards.title: Parts left to others
cards.text: Parts of merged cards left to the founder or lawyer.

next_action.text: Answer the planning questions on your audit report page, then run `/compliance-audit:apply` from the repo root.
next_action.detail: Check first that `gh` is signed in with push access, auto-merge is on, and the ntfy server is set.
